entries.note: The forecast explicitly depends on September 2025 being the peak and is qualified by “likely.”
The lyric follows “As the summary at the top puts it,” making attribution uncertain. It does not establish a literal claim that the bubble has already ended.

entries.test: Whether LLM products or publicly available models continue to exist following the predicted collapse of the AI bubble.
entries.note: The surrounding discussion supports the post-collapse reading; no deadline is stated.

entries.test: Public financial disclosures and deployment studies showing whether LLM technical failures are a major cause of economically unsustainable costs and revenues.
entries.note: This extracts the present causal assertion; the permanent forecast is separately listed.

entries.test: Public financial evidence of sustained, economically viable LLM operations would falsify the claim that their economics will never make sense.
entries.note: The plain economic reading is sustainable commercial viability. “Never” supplies no deadline.

entries.test: Published architecture descriptions and independent reliability evaluations showing whether LLM systems without world models can consistently perform their intended tasks reliably.
entries.note: “AI systems” broadens a statement made in the context of LLMs to all AI.

entries.test: Public financial and deployment evidence showing whether reliability failures constrain profits through lost sales, remediation costs, or restricted commercial uses.
entries.note: In context, the claim concerns profits from LLM-based AI.

entries.test: Research papers and documented model failures predating the post that identify the same core LLM reliability problems.
entries.note: The preceding discussion identifies the relevant problems as longstanding reliability limitations.

entries.test: Public investment estimates through December 2025 together with contemporary evaluations showing whether the core LLM reliability problems persisted.
entries.note: Both the approximate investment total and the persistence of the problems are factual assertions.

entries.test: Research literature, industry statements, surveys, and reporting around publication showing how broadly LLM limitations were understood as inherent rather than temporary.
entries.note: The normalization captures the recognition claim without importing the separate allegation about industry intentions.

entries.test: Public evaluations and deployment outcomes across previously promoted LLM use cases showing whether inherent technical limitations materially impair a substantial share of them.
entries.note: “Undermines” means materially impairs viability, not necessarily makes every affected use impossible.

entries.test: Public evidence of broad investor recognition of LLM limitations followed by contraction in AI valuations, funding, or investment would test the predicted unwinding.
entries.note: The outcome depends on a stated recognition event, with no calendar deadline.
